correctness.rationale: For the precisely stated centrally symmetric Minkowski sum Σ_v[-e_v,e_v]+Σ_edges[-(e_u−e_v),e_u−e_v], a facet with normal 1_S for connected induced S has support |S|+|δ(S)| from the cited Glew construction. Central symmetry permits origin as an optimal Euclidean center, so r=min_S (|S|+|δ(S)|)/sqrt(|S|). For a=|S∩A|,b=|S∩B|,t=a+b, exact cut a(q−b)+b(p−a) is ≥min{pt,n−t}: single-part sets have at least pt outgoing edges, sets meeting both parts have at least n−t. Hence support distance ≥min{(p+1)sqrt t,n/sqrt t}≥min{p+1,sqrt n}. Equality attained only by whole vertex set and min-degree singleton b∈B, with strictness for 1<t<n, yielding all tangent facets and threshold n=(p+1)². A ball of this optimal radius centered c satisfies |sum_(v∈S)c_v|+r sqrt |S|≤|S|+|δ(S)|. Zero-slack normals force c into the claimed common nullspaces (rank 1,q+1,q). All remaining finitely many constraints have positive slack, so small vectors of nullspace produce admissible centers, proving affine span dimensions. Independently checked all (a,b) connected-subset orbits for p=2..5, q from p to 11, and contact-normal ranks in explicit graph cases n<=12. The all-parameter theorem is an exact inequality proof, not finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: An exact Euclidean inradius and full affine-center-locus phase diagram for an infinite natural K_(p,q) family of physically introduced in-in zonotopes is a motivated, nontrivial geometric classification. The transition at q=p²+p+1 changes both contacting facets and the dimension of the optimal-center set, including a smaller intermediate dimension at exact equality. It is not interchangeable with known radii of graphical zonotopes or associahedra.
